tickets.title: Receive actionable HUD events while pi keeps working
tickets.what: In the dispatching pi main session, provide the experience of Claude Code watching `hud watch`. Use native HUD messages, not a foreground wait, editor input, or generic shell. Keep reads and replies explicit through the existing HUD tools.

acceptance.text: A question, block, or report-ready event is available at the next supported model boundary during a run; idle sessions wake and no active tool is cancelled. Routine progress is quiet.
Notices leave drafts untouched and reports unread, belong to the original live session, and retain existing catch-up and shutdown behavior. Claude/Codex delivery is unchanged.
Exercise busy/idle delivery and stale-session filtering in an isolated test and update the pi-specific convention.

accepted.verdict: accepted by the owner; see STATE ledger

tickets.title: Ask the orchestrator without occupying the worker
tickets.what: A pi worker on the HUD role path can post a question and receive its ID without waiting for the decision. Keep the existing synchronous path available for genuine dependencies. Do not change the separate managed protocol or CLI workers.

acceptance.text: The asynchronous tool returns after publication; the worker can do unrelated work while the orchestrator answers through existing `hud_respond`.
An answer wakes or informs only its originating live worker as a native, non-user event; it cannot be delivered twice to that worker, overwrite a draft, or reopen a stopped/replaced session.

An outstanding decision is not mistaken for completion or permission to use its default. Preserve bounded timeout, stop/abort and reporting semantics; dependency-blocked work must not silently proceed.
Test publication, answering during other work and settlement/cleanup with synthetic jobs; document both modes.

accepted.verdict: accepted by the owner; see STATE ledger

tickets.title: Verify asynchronous worker dispatch from the pi main session
tickets.what: A pi main session dispatches an available HUD role, receives the job handle after launch (not after the report), and continues independent work. The role is data: sonic is an example, not a dedicated worker API. Reuse `hud_create`, native watch, `hud_respond` and `hud_read`; do not expand nested-worker permissions.

acceptance.text: Use a non-sonic role (e.g. `imp`). Distinguish launch latency from waiting for settlement. Show the caller doing unrelated work before the report exists, without a foreground wait or status polling.

A question or report-ready event reaches the correct main session at the supported model boundary or wakes it when idle; no editor input or automatic report consumption. Collect the result explicitly.
Record which portions were demonstrated by a synthetic fixture, isolated checks or a live session; do not treat a worker-side helper test as evidence for the main-session path.

accepted.verdict: accepted by the owner; see STATE ledger
